studies.title: Sentence comprehension and voxel-based morphometry in progressive nonfluent aphasia, semantic dementia, and nonaphasic frontotemporal dementia.
studies.abstract: To investigate the basis for impaired sentence comprehension in patients with frontotemporal dementia (FTD) we assessed grammatical comprehension and verbal working memory in 88 patients with three distinct presentations: progressive nonfluent aphasia (PNFA), semantic dementia (SD), and nonaphasic patients with a disorder of social comportment and executive processing (SOC/EXEC). We related sentence comprehension and working memory performance to regional cortical volume in a subgroup of 29 patients with structural MRI scans using voxel-based morphometry. PNFA patients exhibited the greatest difficulty with sentence comprehension and were especially impaired with grammatically complex sentences, which correlated with atrophy in left inferior frontal cortex. Working memory performance in these same patients correlated with a proximal but distinct left inferior frontal region. SD patients' sentence comprehension scores correlated with left inferolateral temporal lobe damage, which we hypothesize and reflect impairments in lexical processing. We did not observe any consistent relationship between cortical atrophy and sentence comprehension impairment in SOC/EXEC patients, suggesting the deficits in this subgroup may be due to more variable declines in executive resources.

studies.abstract: In a multicenter study, FDG-PET images in a population of 29 patients with frontotemporal dementia (FTD) were compared to controls with similar age from each center. studies.title: Non-Fluent Speech in Frontotemporal Lobar Degeneration.
studies.abstract: We investigated the cognitive and neural bases of impaired speech fluency, a central feature of primary progressive aphasia. Speech fluency was assessed in 35 patients with frontotemporal lobar degeneration (FTLD) who presented with progressive non-fluent aphasia (PNFA, n=11), semantic dementia (SemD, n=12), or a social and executive disorder without aphasia (SOC/EXEC, n=12). Fluency was quantified as the number of words per minute in an extended, semi-structured speech sample. This was related to language characteristics of the speech sample and to neuropsychological measures. PNFA patients were significantly less fluent than controls and other FTLD patients. Fluency correlated with grammatical expression but not with speech errors or executive difficulty. SemD and SOC/EXEC patients were also less fluent than controls. In SemD, fluency was associated with semantically limited content. In SOC/EXEC, fluency was associated with executive limitations. Voxel-based morphometry analyses of high-resolution MRI related fluency to gray matter volume in left inferior frontal, insula, and superior temporal regions for the entire cohort of FTLD patients. This region overlapped partially distinct atrophic areas in each FTLD subgroup. It thus appears to play a crucial role in speech fluency, which can be interrupted in different ways in different FTLD subgroups.

The study meets several inclusion criteria: it used VBM as an imaging modality (I3), included a clinically-diagnosed bvFTD sample (N=20) and healthy controls (I4,I5), and reports whole-brain voxelwise VBM results derived from the bvFTD sample (I7). However, it does not report any between-group, whole-brain (voxelwise) bvFTD-versus-control contrasts with peak coordinates in MNI or Talairach space. The imaging results presented are within-group correlations (VBM and DTI correlations with tapping measures) in the bvFTD group rather than voxelwise bvFTD>control or bvFTD<control comparisons, and no peak coordinate table for a bvFTD-versus-control contrast is provided. Therefore inclusion criteria I6 and I8 (at least one between-group contrast comparing bvFTD to controls, and reporting peak coordinates for such a contrast) are not met. No exclusion criteria from the review (E5–E9) apply. Hence the paper must be excluded from the meta-analysis based on missing required between-group coordinate-based results.

The study meets multiple inclusion criteria (I3: uses VBM; I4: clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample; I5: adequate sample sizes with 11 bvFTD and 11 controls; I6: reports between-group voxelwise contrast bvFTD vs controls; I7: provides whole-brain voxelwise group-level results). This full text meets many inclusion criteria for a bvFTD VBM study (I3: uses VBM; I4: includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients [n=14]; I5: bvFTD and control groups each ≥6 participants; I6: reports between-group voxelwise contrasts of bvFTD vs controls; I7: reports whole-brain voxelwise results). This study meets I3 (resting-state fMRI used), I4 (includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group, n=14), and I5 (bvFTD and control groups both ≥6). Excluded because inclusion criterion I8 is not met: the provided full text does not report any explicit peak coordinates (x,y,z in MNI or Talairach) for bvFTD-versus-control whole-brain contrasts. This study uses VBM (voxel-based morphometry) and reports structural imaging analyses, includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample (n=11) and healthy controls (n=14), so I3, I4, and I5 are satisfied. The study meets several inclusion criteria: I3 (uses VBM in addition to DTI), I4 (includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD subgroup), I5 (bvFTD n=12 and controls n=15 meet minimum sample sizes), I6 (reports between-group voxelwise contrasts in MNI standard space comparing each FTD subtype, including bvFTD, to controls), and I7 (reports whole-brain, voxelwise results for the bvFTD group). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are triggered. Because I8 is required and not met, the study must be excluded.

The study meets I3 (uses VBM), I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample), I5 (>=6 patients and >=6 controls), and I7 (reports a whole-brain VBM group comparison). This study meets several inclusion criteria (I3: uses resting-state fMRI; I4: includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients; I5: adequate sample sizes: bvFTD n=27, controls n=48; I6: reports between-group voxelwise contrasts in MNI space; I7: provides whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses). This study reports voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analyses comparing clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients to healthy controls, with whole-brain voxelwise results and peak coordinates reported (e.g., pre-bvFTD vs HC peaks at −62, −2, 16; −2, 54, 8; 46, −4, 4). Sample sizes for the imaging analyses (44 probable bvFTD, 19 possible bvFTD, 14 pre-bvFTD, 36 HC) exceed the minimum. Whole-brain familywise-error–corrected VBM contrasts are presented for probable bvFTD < HC and subgroup contrasts. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, I8), and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

The study uses VBM in a clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample (n=103) and reports whole-brain voxelwise regression results with a peak coordinate (MNI 28,0,0) linking atrophy to reward-seeking. However, it does NOT report any between-group whole-brain (voxelwise) contrast comparing bvFTD patients to healthy controls nor provide peak coordinates for a bvFTD-versus-control contrast. Meta-analysis inclusion criteria I6 and I8 require at least one between-group bvFTD-versus-control contrast with peak coordinates; these are not met. No exclusion criteria apply. Therefore the paper must be excluded.

This study should be excluded because it does not meet the imaging- and result-format inclusion criteria required for the meta-analysis. It used manual region-of-interest structural MRI morphometry of the hypothalamus (ROI tracing and postmortem analyses), not VBM, task/resting fMRI, or FDG-PET (I3 not met). The paper does not report any whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts in a standard stereotactic space nor does it provide peak coordinates (I6, I7, I8 not met). It therefore qualifies for exclusion under E6 (qualifying result comes from a region-of-interest analysis with no unrestricted whole-brain voxelwise result). The study does meet I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample) and I5 (≥6 patients and ≥6 controls). Full text appears complete.

This study includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample (I4) and meets the minimum sample-size criterion (I5: 19 bvFTD patients; control groups ≥6). However, it does not use any of the required imaging modalities (no VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET reported) and therefore fails I3. The paper reports behavioral/neuropsychological task results and lesion-mapping of focal prefrontal stroke patients, but it does not present between-group whole-brain voxelwise contrasts in standard space nor peak coordinates comparing bvFTD to controls (fails I6, I7, I8). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study must be excluded because key imaging and coordinate-reporting inclusion criteria are not met.

This empirical study meets all required inclusion criteria: I3 (uses task-free/resting-state fMRI as a primary imaging modality), I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients), I5 (patient and control sample sizes exceed 6: bvFTD n=17 in main analyses, controls n=19), I6 (reports between-group contrasts comparing bvFTD to controls, e.g., two-sample t tests on HRV–BOLD coupling and other group-level contrasts), I7 (reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses and group differences), and I8 (peak coordinates are reported/referenced for whole-brain bvFTD-versus-control contrasts—see SI Appendix Table S5 referenced in the text). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) apply. The full text provided contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion; supplemental coordinate table is cited. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis.

Although the study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients and uses resting-state fMRI and 18F-FDG PET with sufficient group sizes, it does NOT report any whole-brain, voxelwise bvFTD-versus-control contrasts in stereotactic space with peak coordinates. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I6, I7, and I8. Full text appears complete.

The study meets multiple inclusion criteria: I3 (used voxel-based morphometry), I4 (included clinically diagnosed bvFTD subjects), I5 (patient groups and control group sizes all ≥6), I6 (performed between-group whole-brain VBM contrasts of each disease group vs controls), and I7 (reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise results for target groups). This study does not meet the imaging-modality and reporting requirements for inclusion. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (bvFTD sample included, n=31) and I5 (bvFTD group size ≥6). This paper is a clinical/protocol/experience report describing integrated FDG PET–MRI and illustrative cases (including examples of bvFTD) but does not present group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates. Inclusion not met: I4 (no clearly defined bvFTD sample reported for group analysis with participant counts), I5 (no group sizes ≥6 reported for a bvFTD patient group vs controls), I6 (no between‑group contrasts in MNI/Talairach space), I7 (no whole‑brain group‑level voxelwise results from a bvFTD sample), I8 (no peak coordinates reported). This study uses resting-state fMRI (ICA, fALFF, REHO, seed-based and PLS) and reports whole-brain, voxelwise group analyses. The sample includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD subgroup (n=8) and healthy controls (n=16). The paper reports between-group contrasts including bvFTD versus controls (and bvFTD versus SD) and provides peak coordinates for at least one whole-brain result (e.g., DLPFC peak reported at x=36, y=42, z=30) and references supplementary tables with full between-group coordinate lists. All required whole-brain voxelwise and coordinate reporting criteria appear satisfied, and no exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, review, non-empirical, or only DTI/seed-only methods) are met. Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria.

The paper meets multiple inclusion criteria: I3 (uses FDG‑PET), I4 (clinically diagnosed probable bvFTD sample, N=82), I5 (patient and control groups ≥6; patients N=82, controls N=82), I6 (reports between‑group voxelwise SPM contrasts of bvFTD vs controls), and I7 (reports group‑level, whole‑brain voxelwise results). Therefore it fails to meet inclusion criteria I6, I7, and I8 and meets exclusion criterion E6 (results derive from ROI/mask-based analyses).

This study is excluded because it does not provide the required whole-brain bvFTD versus control voxelwise results or coordinates and uses cortical-thickness/structural morphometry rather than the required VBM/fMRI/FDG-PET modalities. This paper meets multiple inclusion criteria: I3 (uses VBM), I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients), I5 (bvFTD n=19 and controls n=20), I6 (reports between-group VBM contrasts comparing bvFTD to controls), and I7 (reports whole-brain, voxelwise results). This study meets multiple inclusion criteria for the review (it uses VBM, includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients, has adequate sample sizes, and reports whole-brain VBM group contrasts versus controls in MNI space). This is an empirical VBM study that explicitly includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=11) and healthy controls (n=14). The full text reports an empirical VBM study comparing clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=49) to healthy controls (n=30) with whole-brain, voxelwise SPM analyses. The study uses VBM (I3), includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=31) and healthy controls (n=75) meeting sample-size requirements (I4, I5). This is an empirical VBM study of clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients vs. controls with adequate sample sizes and whole-brain voxelwise analyses. The study meets all inclusion criteria: it uses FDG-PET imaging (I3); includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample (n=42) (I4) and healthy controls (n=30) with adequate group sizes (I5); reports whole‑brain voxelwise SPM comparisons of bvFTD versus controls (I6, I7); and references supplementary Table S1 containing precise locations of significant clusters (implying reported peak coordinates in standard space) satisfying the coordinate requirement (I8). The full text reports an empirical resting-state fMRI study that directly includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=12) and healthy controls (n=12). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group contrasts comparing bvFTD versus controls and provides peak coordinates for multiple contrasts (e.g., left angular gyrus –46, –66, 34; right frontoinsula 46, 20, −2; other peaks), satisfying I6, I7 and I8. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED.

Inclusion criteria met: I3 (study uses VBM), I4 (includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group, n=15), I5 (bvFTD n>=6 and controls n>=6), I6 (reports between-group VBM contrasts comparing bvFTD to controls in MNI standard space), I7 (reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level VBM results). The study meets all required inclusion criteria: it uses voxel-based morphometry (FSL-VBM) as the imaging modality; includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants (36 bvFTD, plus 20 bvFTD+ALS) and 23 healthy controls (sample sizes exceed the minimum); reports whole-brain, voxelwise group comparisons (clinical diagnoses vs. controls) and voxelwise correlations; and explicitly references supplementary tables/figures (Supplementary Fig. e1, Tables e2/e3) that report the VBM results. These supplementary materials are acceptable per review rules as the coordinates may be provided there. The bvFTD group is analyzed separately (group comparisons between clinical diagnoses and controls are reported), and whole-brain voxelwise results are described. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not ROI-only, not unrelated modalities).

Although this paper meets several inclusion criteria (uses VBM, includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients, adequate sample sizes, and reports whole-brain voxelwise bvFTD-versus-control contrasts in MNI space), the provided full text does not report any peak coordinates (x,y,z in MNI or Talairach) for the whole-brain bvFTD-versus-control contrasts. Inclusion criterion I8 (reporting of actual peak coordinates) is therefore not satisfied based on the available material. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are met. The supplementary material might contain coordinates, but it is not present in the provided full text, so exclusion is based on missing coordinates per I8.

This study is excluded because it does not meet the imaging- and whole-brain coordinate requirements of the review. Exclusion criteria met: E6 (results derive from region-of-interest analyses and no unrestricted whole-brain voxelwise contrast is reported) and E9 (study reports cortical thickness/ROI-based analyses rather than VBM, task/resting fMRI, or FDG-PET). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (bvFTD patients were clinically diagnosed and included) and I5 (bvFTD n=18 and controls n=20, both ≥6). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (imaging modality is FreeSurfer cortical thickness/ROI MRI, not VBM/fMRI/FDG-PET), I6 (no between-group whole-brain contrast in stereotaxic space comparing bvFTD to controls is reported), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise result identified for the target sample), and I8 (no peak coordinates in MNI/Talairach space are reported). Full text appears complete and contains methods/results/discussion (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This study does not meet key inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. Although it uses voxel-wise gray-matter (VBM-style) analysis of structural MRI (I3), includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD patient group (n=18) (I4) and meets the minimum patient group size (I5), it does not report a between-group whole-brain contrast comparing bvFTD to healthy controls (I6 not met). The reported whole-brain results are multivariate SVM weight maps identifying regions that contribute to classification (interpretable as whole-brain results; I7 met), but the manuscript (as provided) does not report any peak coordinates (x,y,z) for a bvFTD-versus-control whole-brain contrast nor for the SVM weight-map peaks in MNI/Talairach space (I8 not met). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are triggered. Because the meta-analysis requires explicit whole-brain bvFTD-versus-control contrasts with reported peak coordinates, this paper must be excluded.

The study uses VBM (I3), includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD subgroup (n=27) (I4), and has >=6 patients in the bvFTD group and >=6 healthy controls (I5). However, the full text does not present a clear whole-brain, between-group bvFTD-versus-control contrast with reported peak coordinates in MNI or Talairach space. While the authors state that they compared each diagnostic group to controls and reference an online supplemental table, the provided full text only reports peak coordinates for a correlation across all patient groups (anosognosia correlation: e.g., MNI 61, -35, 2) and does not include any explicit bvFTD vs control voxelwise contrast peaks or a group-level whole-brain result identified as coming solely from the bvFTD sample. Therefore the manuscript fails to satisfy I6, I7 and I8 (no clearly reported bvFTD-versus-control whole-brain contrast with coordinates). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are triggered by the provided text.

Although this is an empirical VBM study including a well-characterised bvFTD sample, it does not provide any bvFTD-versus-healthy-control whole-brain voxelwise contrasts. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses Voxel-Based Morphometry), I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD subjects), I5 (bvFTD group size ≥6). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I6 (no reported bvFTD vs control contrast), I7 (no whole-brain group-level result identified as coming from the bvFTD vs control target sample), I8 (no peak coordinates for a bvFTD-versus-control whole-brain contrast). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) apply. Therefore the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis that requires bvFTD-versus-control whole-brain coordinates.

The study is a retrospective case series of 8 patients with FBSS who were clinically diagnosed as FTD and had FDG-PET/SPECT in some cases. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses FDG-PET), I4 (participants were clinically diagnosed bvFTD/FTD), I5 (patient group n=8 ≥6). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no between-group bvFTD-versus-control voxelwise contrasts reported), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise results identified for the target sample), I8 (no peak coordinates in MNI/Talairach reported). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) apply. The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study must be excluded because it lacks the required whole-brain, coordinate-based voxelwise between-group analyses (I6–I8 not satisfied).

This study meets the review objectives and all inclusion criteria: it uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and FDG-PET (I3), includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample (23 probable/possible bvFTD patients) (I4), and the patient (n=23) and control groups exceed the minimum sample sizes (>6) (I5). The paper reports between-group voxelwise contrasts comparing bvFTD versus controls using SPM8 with images normalized to MNI space (I6,I7). The methods state that results were reported in MNI coordinates and refer to tables/figures (including supplemental tables S2/S3) where peak coordinates are presented (I8). Whole-brain, voxelwise analyses are described (not ROI-limited), and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This study uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and reports whole-brain, group-level comparisons of a clinically diagnosed bvFTD cohort (N=66) versus controls (N=30), satisfying I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7. However, the provided full text does not report any peak coordinates (x,y,z in MNI or Talairach space) for the bvFTD-versus-control voxelwise contrasts or subtype comparisons, and no coordinate table or numeric peak locations are present in the main text or figure captions excerpted here. Because inclusion criterion I8 (explicit peak coordinates for at least one whole-brain bvFTD-versus-control contrast) is not met, the study cannot be included for coordinate-based meta-analysis. The full text appears otherwise complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion), so I set fulltext_incomplete=false. Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4, I5, I6, I7. Inclusion criteria not met: I8. Exclusion criteria met: none ([])

This study uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and reports whole-brain group-level contrasts for clinical subgroups including behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD). It provides peak coordinates for bvFTD versus controls (e.g., [4, 20, 46]) and presents voxelwise SPM results and conjunction analyses. The study includes a healthy control group (n=25) and a clinical patient cohort (n=18) and reports bvFTD-specific results (bvFTD vs controls) rather than pooling bvFTD with other syndromes. Therefore it meets imaging modality (I3), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD (I4), reports sufficient sample sizes overall and a control group (I5), contains between-group bvFTD-vs-control contrasts (I6), provides whole-brain voxelwise results for the target group (I7), and supplies peak coordinates for the bvFTD contrast (I8). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I8 (no peak coordinates reported for whole-brain bvFTD-versus-control VBM contrasts in the provided full text). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (VBM used), I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample), I5 (sufficient sample sizes: 16 bvFTD, 22 controls), I6 (between-group VBM contrasts vs. controls in MNI space were performed), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise group-level results reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I8 (no explicit peak coordinates reported in MNI/Talairach for bvFTD>control or control>bvFTD contrasts in the supplied full text). Exclusion criteria met: none (E5- E9 not applicable). Full text appears complete. Because I8 is required, the study must be excluded from the coordinate-based meta-analysis despite otherwise satisfying other criteria.

Excluded because although the study used voxel-based morphometry (satisfies I3) and the overall sample included some clinically diagnosed bvFTD cases within the cohort (satisfies I4), it does not report a bvFTD-specific between-group whole-brain voxelwise contrast versus controls. The imaging results are presented by FTLD-TDP pathological subtype (type 1/2/3), not as a bvFTD-defined group; therefore there is no bvFTD-versus-control contrast (fails I6 and I7). The paper does not provide peak coordinates for any bvFTD-versus-control whole-brain contrast (fails I8). Nor does it report a distinct bvFTD patient group with at least 6 participants for a dedicated bvFTD contrast (fails I5). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are met.

This study is excluded because, although it includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=20) and acquired FDG-PET for diagnostic support, the paper does not report any whole-brain voxelwise group-level imaging analyses (VBM, task/resting fMRI, or FDG-PET) comparing bvFTD to controls, nor does it provide peak coordinates in MNI/Talairach space. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD present) and I5 (bvFTD n>=6). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no imaging modality analysis reported for group comparisons beyond use for diagnosis), I6 (no between-group voxelwise contrasts in defined stochastic space), I7 (no whole-brain group-level voxelwise result reported), I8 (no peak coordinates provided). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This study includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample (n=14) and healthy controls (n=22), and uses a VBM-based measure of anterior cingulate gray matter, so it meets I3 (VBM used), I4 (bvFTD sample), and I5 (sample sizes >=6). However, the paper does not report any unrestricted, group-level whole-brain voxelwise bvFTD-versus-control contrasts with peak coordinates in MNI or Talairach space. The VBM procedure was applied to extract mean gray matter density within an anterior cingulate mask (ROI/mask-based individual measures) rather than reporting whole-brain voxelwise group results, and no peak coordinates are provided. Therefore it fails I6, I7, and I8. This places the study into exclusion criterion E6 (results come from a region-of-interest/masked analysis with no unrestricted whole-brain voxelwise result). Full text appears complete. Exclusion reason: E6. Inclusion met: I3, I4, I5. Inclusion not met: I6, I7, I8.

This study investigates bvFTD using FDG-PET and DTI (and applied VBM), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=30) and healthy controls (n=42), and reports voxelwise, whole-brain DTI/GM analyses after spatial normalization to MNI space. However, the manuscript does not report any peak coordinates (x,y,z in MNI or Talairach space) for the reported whole-brain bvFTD-versus-control contrasts. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses FDG-PET and VBM), I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample), I5 (>=6 patients and controls), I6 (voxelwise/group contrasts in defined space), I7 (reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise results). Inclusion criterion not met: I8 (no peak coordinates provided). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study must be excluded because it fails to provide the required peak coordinates (I8).

The study reports voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analyses in a bvFTD sample (satisfying I3, I4) with large patient numbers (satisfying I5). However, the reported whole-brain VBM comparison is between bvFTD and a parallel mild-AD cohort (bvFTD vs AD), not bvFTD versus healthy/control participants, so it does not meet the requirement for a bvFTD-versus-controls contrast (I6). In addition, no peak coordinates (MNI or Talairach) for a bvFTD-versus-control whole-brain contrast are provided in the full text, so criterion I8 is not met. Therefore the paper does not satisfy all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This empirical study used whole-brain VBM (structural MRI) and FDG-PET (I3) and included clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients per published criteria (I4). Patient group sizes exceed thresholds (23 bvFTD; MRI/PET after QC: 21/23) and controls are sufficient (I5). The paper reports direct between-group voxelwise contrasts of bvFTD versus healthy controls in MNI space with conversion to Talairach and refers to peak maxima coordinates in Tables 2 and 3 (I6, I7, I8). Analyses are whole-brain voxelwise (not ROI-only) and there is no indication of exclusion criteria being met (e.g., review, non-empirical, ROI-only, or predominantly other diagnoses). The full article text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; referenced tables contain stereotactic peaks. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria apply.

Excluded because the reported voxelwise morphometry results were restricted to a merged subcortical grey-matter mask (i.e., an ROI-based voxelwise analysis), and the manuscript does not provide an unrestricted whole-brain voxelwise bvFTD-versus-control contrast with peak coordinates. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (VBM-type voxelwise morphometry was performed), I4 (a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group is included, n=10), I5 (bvFTD group and controls meet sample size requirements), I6 (between-group contrasts of phenotype groups vs controls are reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I7 (no whole-brain, unrestricted voxelwise result for the bvFTD group is reported), I8 (no peak coordinates for a whole-brain bvFTD>control contrast are provided in the supplied full text). Exclusion criteria applied: E6 (qualifying results come from an analysis confined to an anatomical mask; no unrestricted whole-brain voxelwise result is available). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical VBM study that includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=18) and healthy controls (n=27). The authors report whole-brain, voxelwise bvFTD-versus-control contrasts (age included as nuisance) with results corrected for multiple comparisons and provide peak coordinates in MNI space (e.g., bvFTD: x=8, y=28, z=-28). The paper therefore meets imaging modality (VBM), sample, sample size, between-group contrast, whole-brain evidence, and coordinate-reporting criteria. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not ROI-only, not other modalities only, and bvFTD cases are separable). Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

(a) Exclusion IDs met: none. (b) Inclusion IDs met: I3 (FDG-PET was used), I4 (study included clinically diagnosed behavioral variant FTD patients), I5 (patient group has ≥6 bvFTD cases—20 FTD patients total; control group ≥6). (c) Inclusion IDs not met: I6 (no reported between-group whole-brain voxelwise contrast comparing bvFTD group to controls in MNI/Talairach space), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise results identified for the bvFTD group), I8 (no peak coordinates reported for any bvFTD-versus-control whole-brain contrast). The full text is complete. Because key meta-analysis requirements (voxelwise group contrasts and reported coordinates) are absent, this study does not provide the required spatial coordinate data and must be excluded.

This study is excluded because it does not meet key inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients), I5 (bvFTD group n=11 ≥6), I7 (reports whole-brain voxelwise analyses identified as coming from the bvFTD sample). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I3 (imaging modality is tensor-based morphometry (TBM) derived from T1 MRI, not VBM, task/resting-state fMRI, or FDG-PET), I6 (between-group contrasts are bvFTD vs early-onset AD rather than bvFTD vs healthy controls as required), and I8 (no peak coordinates in MNI/Talairach space are reported for any whole-brain bvFTD-versus-control contrast). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Given failure to satisfy modality and coordinate requirements, the paper must be excluded from the coordinate-based meta-analysis.

The study is excluded because it does not meet required imaging-modality and coordinate-reporting inclusion criteria. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (contains clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients), I5 (bvFTD n=9 and controls n=18), I6 (reports between-group voxelwise contrasts using TBSS/Randomise in standard space), and I7 (reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise WM results for the bvFTD group). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I3 (does NOT use VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET — modalities are DTI, structural ROI volumetry, and ASL perfusion), and I8 (no peak MNI/Talairach coordinates are reported for bvFTD-versus-control whole-brain contrasts). No exclusion criteria from the protocol are triggered (e.g., the paper is empirical and not a review, and results are not ROI-only since TBSS voxelwise results are reported). Because two required inclusion items (I3 and I8) are unmet, the study must be excluded.

The full text is complete. This study is excluded because, although it includes bvFTD patients and uses FDG-PET (I3, I4) and has sufficient patient numbers (n=27) (I5), it does not report any whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts of bvFTD versus healthy controls in a defined stereotactic space, nor does it provide peak coordinates. Specifically, the imaging analyses were visual ratings of MRI and FDG-PET and consensus clinical interpretation rather than VBM/fMRI/voxelwise FDG-PET statistic maps with MNI/Talairach peak coordinates. Therefore inclusion criteria I6, I7, and I8 are not met. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) apply. Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4, I5. Inclusion criteria not met: I6, I7, I8. Exclusion criteria met: none ([]).

The study reports a VBM analysis comparing clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=26) to healthy controls (n=23) and provides whole-brain voxelwise results described as clusters in MNI space. However, the provided full text does not include any explicit peak coordinates (x,y,z) for the bvFTD-versus-control voxelwise contrasts; coordinates may exist in supplementary material or tables not included here. Therefore inclusion criterion I8 (peak coordinates reported) is not satisfied. No exclusion criteria are met based on the provided content.

While this study uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample (24 bvFTD patients) with sufficient group size, it does NOT report any between-group whole-brain contrasts comparing the bvFTD group to healthy controls. The VBM results are presented as voxelwise correlations of insight-discrepancy scores across a mixed patient cohort and domain-wise covariation analyses; the authors state that separate analyses within individual patient groups produced no significant results. Therefore the study satisfies I3 (VBM used), I4 (bvFTD patients included), and I5 (bvFTD group n>=6), but fails I6 (no bvFTD vs control whole-brain contrast), I7 (no group-level whole-brain result identified as coming from the bvFTD target group), and I8 (no peak coordinates reported for a bvFTD-versus-control contrast). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This study used FDG-PET (I3) and included clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients after follow-up (I4) with at least 15 bvFTD cases (I5). However, it does not report any group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) bvFTD-versus-control contrasts, nor does it present peak coordinates in MNI/Talairach space. Results are qualitative (visual reads) and diagnostic accuracy metrics, not voxelwise statistical maps or coordinate tables. Therefore inclusion criteria I6, I7, and I8 are not met, and the study cannot contribute coordinates for coordinate-based meta-analysis. Full text appears complete. Exclusion criterion applied: E6 (no unrestricted whole-brain voxelwise result reported / qualifying result not a whole-brain voxelwise contrast).

This study is excluded because it uses cortical thickness (surface-based FreeSurfer) and subcortical volume analyses rather than the imaging modalities required by the review (VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET), and the review's exclusion criterion E9 (cortical thickness methods) therefore applies. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients), I5 (bvFTD group n=37 and controls n=33, both ≥6), and I7 (reports whole-brain vertex-wise surface analyses identified for the bvFTD group). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (imaging modality is cortical thickness/FreeSurfer, not VBM/fMRI/FDG-PET), I6 and I8 (no peak MNI/Talairach coordinates for whole-brain bvFTD-versus-control contrasts are provided in the supplied full text; coordinates appear not to be reported in the main text). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore excluded based on E9.

This empirical study reports whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analyses including bvFTD patients versus healthy controls, with MNI stereotaxic coordinates provided for results. The sample includes 12 clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients and 12 controls (both ≥6). The paper presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (bvFTD vs. Controls) and explicitly states that maximum coordinates are provided in MNI space. Imaging modality (VBM), patient sample, sample sizes, whole-brain voxelwise results, and reported coordinates satisfy the meta-analysis inclusion criteria. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, and supplemental references).

The study meets multiple inclusion criteria (uses VBM; includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients; sample sizes: 15 bvFTD, 19 controls; reports whole-brain group comparisons and voxelwise analyses in MNI space). However the full text as provided does not report peak coordinates (x,y,z in MNI or Talairach space) for any bvFTD-versus-control whole-brain contrast; reported numeric coordinates are for a brain–behavior regression (intentionality vs GM) rather than the between-group atrophy contrast. Inclusion criterion I8 (explicit peak coordinates for at least one whole-brain bvFTD-versus-control contrast) is therefore not satisfied, which prevents inclusion. Full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met.

Although this study uses FDG-PET (I3), enrolls a clinically diagnosed probable bvFTD sample (n=17) meeting the minimum sample size (I4, I5), and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise SPM results (I7), it does not report an explicit between-group bvFTD-versus-controls contrast in MNI/Talairach space (I6 not met). The analyses are based on single-subject contrasts versus a normative database and one-sample group tests derived from those contrasts rather than a direct between-group contrast against a contemporaneous control group. Crucially, no peak coordinates (x,y,z) for any whole-brain bvFTD-versus-control contrast are provided in the text, tables, or figure captions (I8 not met). Therefore the study fails the coordinate-reporting requirement and cannot be included.

This study meets several inclusion criteria: I3 (FDG‑PET was used), I4 (includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group), I5 (bvFTD N=24 and controls N=32), I6 (between‑group contrasts bvFTD vs controls in SPM normalized to MNI space), and I7 (reports whole‑brain voxelwise group analyses). However I8 is not met in the provided full text: no peak coordinates (x,y,z in MNI or Talairach space) for any bvFTD-versus-control whole‑brain contrast are reported in the text supplied (only anatomical cluster descriptions). I found no tables or figure captions containing coordinates in the provided content; coordinates may exist in supplementary materials online, but they are not present here for verification. Therefore the paper cannot be included under the meta-analysis rules requiring reported peak coordinates.

This VBM study includes a clearly defined bvFTD patient sample (n=22) and age-matched controls (n=17), uses voxel-based morphometry as the imaging modality, and reports voxel-wise group-level contrasts and covariate analyses with results described in MNI space (the methods state that maximum coordinates are reported in MNI coordinates). The patient and control groups each exceed the minimum sample size (>=6). The paper reports group-level voxelwise atrophy contrasts comparing bvFTD to controls and provides peak coordinates for significant clusters (reported in the methods and results), satisfying whole-brain voxelwise reporting requirements. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not restricted to ROI-only results without whole-brain contrasts, not other imaging modality-only, and bvFTD cases are a separable target group). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This study is excluded because it does not use the required imaging modalities (I3 not met): it uses structural longitudinal MRI with tensor-based morphometry and boundary-shift integral rather than VBM, fMRI, or FDG‑PET. It also does not report any bvFTD-versus-control whole-brain voxelwise contrasts with peak coordinates and does not include a healthy control group for such contrasts (I6, I7, I8 not met). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants are included) and I5 (patient group sizes exceed 6). No exclusion criteria are triggered. Full text appears complete and contains methods, results, and discussion supporting these determinations.

This is an empirical FDG-PET study of clinically diagnosed bv‐FTD patients (final sample n=8) versus healthy controls (n=26). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise SPM group contrasts comparing bv‐FTD to controls with FWE-corrected results and refers to peak coordinates (reported in Table III) for significant clusters (bv‐FTD < controls). Imaging modality (FDG‐PET), target sample (bv‐FTD), adequate sample sizes (≥6 per group), presence of between-group voxelwise contrasts in a defined statistical space, whole-brain group-level results, and reported peak coordinates satisfy the review inclusion criteria. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so is complete for screening. No exclusion criteria (e.g., review, ROI-only analysis, wrong modality, or mixed-diagnosis pooling) are met.

Full text reports VBM analyses comparing bvFTD (n=16) to controls (n=17) and provides whole-brain voxelwise atrophy results; thus I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are satisfied. However, the provided full text does not include any peak coordinates (x,y,z) for the bvFTD-versus-control whole-brain contrasts — those coordinates appear to be referenced as being in Supplementary Tables/Figures which are not present here. Because I cannot confirm the presence of peak coordinates (I8), the record fails to meet all required inclusion criteria. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) apply based on the available text. As supplementary material likely contains the coordinates but is missing from the provided full text, I mark fulltext_incomplete=true and exclude pending access to the complete article (including supplements) that contains the reported coordinates.

This study uses FDG-PET (I3 met), includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=11) (I4 met), and has >=6 participants in patient and control groups (I5 met). However, it does NOT report any whole-brain, between-group voxelwise contrast directly comparing bvFTD versus healthy controls with peak coordinates in MNI/Talairach space. The PET analyses reported are voxelwise regression correlations across all subjects with deficit scores and group-difference comments are reported from extracted regional values (non-voxelwise). Therefore inclusion criteria I6, I7 and I8 are not satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are triggered. Full text appears complete. Exclusion reason: fails to provide a bvFTD-versus-control whole-brain voxelwise contrast with reported peak coordinates (I6, I7, I8 not met).

This study is excluded because it does not provide whole-brain voxelwise results or peak coordinates required for coordinate-based meta-analysis. (a) Exclusion criteria met: E6 (results are ROI/tract-based and no unrestricted whole-brain voxelwise contrasts are reported) and E9 (primary imaging results are DTI tractography and ROI-based resting-state fMRI connectivity rather than VBM, whole-brain fMRI voxelwise maps, or FDG-PET). (b) Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses resting-state fMRI as an imaging modality), I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients), I5 (bvFTD and control groups each >=6 participants). (c) Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no reported between-group voxelwise contrast in MNI/Talairach space), I7 (no whole-brain voxelwise group-level result), I8 (no peak coordinates reported). Full text appears complete. Therefore EXCLUDED.

This study is excluded because its VBM results were derived from an a priori PFC/MTL region-of-interest mask rather than an unrestricted whole-brain voxelwise analysis, meeting exclusion criterion E6. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (VBM imaging), I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample present), I5 (bvFTD n=22 and controls n=38, both ≥6), I6 (between-group bvFTD vs control contrasts reported), and I8 (peak coordinates reported in MNI space). Inclusion criterion not met: I7 (requires at least one group-level whole-brain voxelwise result from the target sample; the paper reports only ROI-masked voxelwise results). Full text appears complete.

The study is excluded because it does not report whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts in a standard stereotactic space nor report peak coordinates. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses [18F]FDG-PET), I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD cases), I5 (bvFTD patient group n=27 ≥6). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no reported between-group contrast in MNI/Talairach space comparing bvFTD to controls), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise result), I8 (no peak coordinates reported). The imaging analyses were visual/readings and diagnostic accuracy metrics (sensitivity/specificity), not voxelwise or coordinate-based results. Full text appears complete and sufficient to make this determination.

This study is excluded because it does not report any between-group bvFTD-versus-control contrast with reported peak coordinates in MNI/Talairach space. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses FDG-PET), I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample), I5 (≥6 bvFTD patients; n=37), I7 (reports whole-brain voxelwise group-level analyses within the bvFTD sample relating occupation to FDG metabolism). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no explicit between-group bvFTD vs. control contrast in stereotactic space is reported), I8 (no peak coordinates for any whole-brain bvFTD-versus-control contrast are provided in the text). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) apply. Full text appears complete for screening purposes.

Although this study uses VBM (I3) in a clinically-diagnosed bvFTD sample (I4) with n=20 patients (I5), it does NOT report any between-group bvFTD-versus-control whole-brain voxelwise contrasts in MNI/Talairach space. The reported results are within-group correlations between gray-matter volume and SEA subscores in the bvFTD group (some reported as peak coordinates), and the imaging analyses were performed inside an a priori frontal mask (region-restricted analysis). Therefore the study fails to meet I6 (no bvFTD vs. control contrast), I7 (no whole‑brain group-level voxelwise result vs controls), and I8 (no peak coordinates for a bvFTD-versus-control contrast). Because the qualifying results are confined to an anatomical mask (ROI-restricted VBM), exclusion criterion E6 applies. Full text appears complete.

While this is an empirical MRI study of clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=28) with healthy controls (n=26), it does not use VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET. The study uses manual ROI-based segmentation and surface/shape analysis (SPHARM-PDM) of the caudate and putamen rather than whole-brain voxelwise analyses. No whole-brain, voxelwise bvFTD-versus-control contrasts in a standard stereotaxic space (MNI/Talairach) are reported, and no peak coordinates are provided. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I3, I6, I7, and I8. Additionally, the qualifying results are ROI-based (striatal volume/shape), meeting exclusion criterion E6 (region-of-interest analysis without unrestricted whole-brain voxelwise results). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample) and I5 (sample sizes ≥6). Given these mismatches with the meta-analysis imaging and reporting requirements, the study should be excluded.

Excluded because the study reports only diffusion tensor imaging (DTI/TBSS) and seed-based resting-state fMRI connectivity analyses rather than VBM, task fMRI, or FDG-PET whole-brain voxelwise contrasts required for inclusion; this meets exclusion criterion E9. The study does meet multiple inclusion criteria: I3 (uses resting-state fMRI), I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients), I5 (sample sizes: 12 bvFTD, 17 controls), I6 (reports between-group contrasts of bvFTD vs controls), and I7 (performs whole-brain voxelwise analyses). However it does not satisfy I8 because no peak coordinates (MNI/Talairach x,y,z) for bvFTD-versus-control whole-brain contrasts are presented in the provided full text (they are only referenced as Supplementary Tables/Figures without coordinates in the main text). Therefore the paper must be excluded.

This study should be excluded because it does not meet the imaging-modality and whole-brain coordinate reporting requirements of the review. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (sample includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients) and I5 (patient and control groups each have ≥6 participants). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (imaging modality is structural MRI volumetry using Freesurfer, not VBM, task/resting fMRI, or FDG‑PET), I6 (no between-group contrast reported in a standard stereotactic space like MNI/Talairach), I7 (no whole‑brain voxelwise group-level result reported; analyses are ROI/volume-based), and I8 (no peak coordinates reported for any bvFTD‑vs‑control whole‑brain contrast). Exclusion criteria met: E6 (results derive from region-of-interest/ROI volumetric analyses rather than unrestricted whole‑brain voxelwise analyses). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore EXCLUDED.

This study reports whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analyses comparing a clinically diagnosed behavioural-variant FTD (bvFTD) patient group to healthy controls. The bvFTD group (n=10) and control group (n=14) each exceed the minimum sample-size threshold. VBM (an accepted imaging modality per I3) was used and voxel-wise group contrasts versus controls are presented. Results are reported in MNI space with peak coordinates provided in the tables (e.g., Table 4 and Table 5), and whole-brain, voxelwise covariate analyses are described. The bvFTD group is analyzed separately (not pooled) for bvFTD-versus-control contrasts. The full text contains methods, results, and discussion, and is complete for screening. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only analysis, non-empirical paper, inappropriate sample, or disallowed imaging modality) are met.

The study meets inclusion criteria I3 (uses VBM/anatomical MRI and resting-state fMRI), I4 (includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group, n=23), and I5 (bvFTD n≥6 and control n≥6). However it does NOT meet I6–I8: the provided full text, while reporting voxel-wise processing and regional findings, does not report any whole-brain peak coordinates (x,y,z in MNI or Talairach) for bvFTD-versus-control contrasts, nor explicit whole-brain voxelwise result tables or coordinate lists. Inclusion criterion I8 (required peak coordinates) is therefore not satisfied; consequently I6 and I7 (reporting between-group contrasts in defined space and a clearly-identified whole-brain group-level voxelwise result) are also not met. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) apply. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false). Because failure to provide peak coordinates (I8) is mandatory, the paper must be excluded from the coordinate-based meta-analysis.

This full text meets the review objective and required inclusion criteria. Imaging modality: whole-brain VBM on structural MRI (I3). Sample includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (N=50) within the FTD-spectrum (I4) and age-matched controls are reported; group sizes exceed the 6-participant minimum (I5). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses identified as coming from the target sample (FTD and syndrome-specific bvFTD) (I7). Syndrome-specific (bvFTD) whole-brain contrasts and resulting peak coordinates in MNI space are provided (reported in text/Tables/Figures; Table 4 and figure captions), satisfying the requirement for at least one between-group contrast with coordinates (I6, I8). No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, uses VBM, bvFTD separable, empirical data present). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This full-text reports whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analyses comparing a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=24) to cognitively normal controls (n=179). Imaging modality is VBM on structural MRI. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (bvFTD vs controls and interaction effects) and provides peak coordinates in MNI space for multiple significant clusters (e.g., MNI = 12,18,9; 30,-7,-15; -46,36,15). Both patient and control groups exceed the minimum size of 6. The bvFTD group is analyzed separately (not pooled). The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria (reviews, ROI-only results, non-empirical, wrong modality, or mixed-diagnosis predominance) are met. Therefore the study satisfies all required inclusion criteria.

Exclude per E7: the study’s patient groups are primary progressive aphasia (PPA) variants and Alzheimer’s disease, not behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick’s disease. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (sample size requirement: patient group n=6 PPA; control group n=8). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (modality is dual-phase 18F-florbetapir PET, not VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET), I4 (does not include clinically diagnosed bvFTD/Pick’s disease), I6 (no between-group contrast comparing a bvFTD group to controls), I7 (no whole-brain group-level voxelwise result identified as coming from a bvFTD target group), I8 (no peak coordinates reported for a bvFTD-versus-control contrast). This study meets I3 (uses FDG-PET), I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients within the sample: 7 bvFTD plus related variants), and I5 (>=6 patients and >=6 controls after data exclusion). Group analyses are ROI-based and the voxelwise analyses described are single-subject (patient vs controls) maps; no peak coordinates or a whole-brain group-level SPM contrast are provided. Therefore it fails I6, I7, and I8 and falls under exclusion E6 (qualifying results come from ROI or non-whole-brain analyses). Full text appears complete. Exclusion IDs met: E6. Inclusion IDs met: I3, I4, I5. Inclusion IDs not met: I6, I7, I8.

Study meets imaging and sample size criteria (uses VBM; includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients, N=18; healthy controls N=34) but does NOT report a whole-brain, voxelwise bvFTD-versus-control between-group contrast with peak coordinates. This paper meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis: it used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) as the imaging modality; included a clinically-diagnosed bvFTD patient group (n=24) and healthy controls (n=22), both above the minimum N=6; reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level contrasts comparing bvFTD to controls; and provides peak coordinates in MNI space (the text states maximum coordinates were provided, and specific MNI coordinates are reported, e.g., overlap at x=-38,y=30,z=-10). Study meets several inclusion criteria: it uses VBM and resting-state/task fMRI (I3), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=14) and controls (n=19) meeting sample-size requirements (I4, I5), reports between-group VBM contrasts and whole-brain voxelwise analyses comparing bvFTD to controls (I6, I7). This full text meets all inclusion criteria: I3 - Voxel-based morphometry (VBM) was used for grey-matter analyses; I4 - includes a clinician-diagnosed bvFTD group (n=18); I5 - sample sizes meet thresholds (bvFTD n=18, healthy controls n=18); I6 - reports between-group voxelwise contrasts comparing controls > bvFTD (bvFTD not pooled with other patient groups); I7 - whole-brain, group-level voxelwise VBM results are reported (FWE-corrected clusters, full-brain contrasts); I8 - the manuscript reports anatomical results in main-text tables and supplementary tables and uses MNI space (Table 2 and Supplementary Table 1 are cited, with MNI noted), indicating peak coordinates are provided for voxelwise contrasts/correlations. The study meets several inclusion criteria (I3: uses VBM; I4: includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=11); I5: sample sizes meet minimums for patient and control groups; I6: reports between-group voxelwise contrasts in MNI space). Full text appears complete. Exclusion summary: E6 applied; Inclusions met: I3, I4, I5, I6; Inclusions not met: I7, I8.

The study is excluded because it does not report any whole-brain, group-level bvFTD-versus-control voxelwise contrasts with peak coordinates. The study meets several inclusion criteria: it uses VBM and FDG-PET (I3); the patient sample is clinically diagnosed FTD where semantic dementia and progressive nonfluent aphasia were explicitly excluded (consistent with bvFTD/binary FTD group) (I4); sample sizes meet the threshold (13 FTD patients, 20 controls) (I5); the analyses are whole-brain, voxelwise SPM comparisons normalized to MNI space, reporting group-level voxelwise contrasts (I6, I7). (a) Exclusion criteria met: E6 (results derive from ROI-based/parcellation analyses without reporting unrestricted whole-brain voxelwise results). This is an empirical imaging study that meets all inclusion criteria: it uses FDG-PET and voxel-based morphometry (I3); includes clinically diagnosed behavioural-variant FTD patients (n=24) (I4); has ≥6 patients and ≥6 controls (patients n=24, controls n=12) (I5); reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise VBM analyses (SPM) (I7) and explicitly references peak coordinates (MNI coordinate reported in text and ‘see supplementary information for exact coordinates’) (I6,I8). This study should be excluded because, although it uses VBM (I3), includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=20) (I4), and has adequate sample sizes for patient and control groups (I5), it does NOT report any bvFTD-versus-control whole-brain voxelwise group contrasts in MNI/Talairach space nor does it provide peak coordinates. Although the study clearly uses VBM (I3), includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=19) and controls (n=19) meeting the sample-size requirement (I4, I5), and reports whole-brain, group-level VBM contrasts comparing bvFTD versus controls in MNI space (I6, I7), the provided full-text does not include any peak coordinate values (x,y,z) for the bvFTD-versus-control whole-brain contrasts. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) apply to the available content. Because the coordinate requirement (I8) cannot be confirmed from the supplied text, I must exclude this record. Full text appears otherwise complete, but the absence of reported peak coordinates and the use of cortical thickness analysis lead to exclusion under E9.

This study is excluded because it does not meet the imaging-modality and whole-brain voxelwise coordinate reporting requirements. Although this study meets several inclusion criteria (uses VBM; includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients; has sufficient sample sizes; reports whole-brain voxelwise group contrasts including bvFTD vs. controls), the provided full text does not report any peak coordinates (x,y,z in MNI or Talairach space) for bvFTD-versus-control or other whole-brain contrasts. Although this study uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients within a large neurodegenerative sample (satisfying I3, I4, I5), it does not report any whole-brain, voxelwise bvFTD-versus-control group contrasts nor provide peak coordinates for such a contrast. The bvFTD-specific analyses reported are restricted ROI analyses within the insula and main VBM results relate to presence of disgusting behaviors and disgust recognition across a heterogeneous patient sample rather than an explicit bvFTD vs control whole-brain comparison. This study should be excluded. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses FDG-PET) and I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients). The paper meets several inclusion criteria (uses voxel-based morphometry; includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients; sample sizes meet thresholds; reports between-group contrasts and whole-brain voxelwise analyses). This study meets many inclusion criteria: it used voxel-based morphometry and task/resting-state fMRI (I3); included clinically diagnosed behavioural-variant FTD patients (I4); patient and control groups meet the minimum sample sizes (I5); it reports whole-brain between-group voxelwise contrasts in MNI space (I6,I7). This is an empirical multimodal imaging study that includes 11 bvFTD patients and uses VBM, resting-state fMRI (degree centrality), and FDG-PET (I3, I4, I5 satisfied). The analyses focus on ROI-derived voxelwise measures from predefined network cores and SVM classification between patient groups; results are reported as classification accuracies rather than standard whole-brain/between-group statistical maps with peak coordinates. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I6, I7, and I8, and meets exclusion criterion E6 (qualifying results come from ROI-based analyses without unrestricted whole-brain voxelwise bvFTD-vs-control contrasts). This study uses FDG-PET and includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=13), but it does not report any whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts in stereotactic (MNI/Talairach) space nor does it provide peak coordinates. This study meets several inclusion criteria: I3 (used voxel-based morphometry), I4 (included clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients), I5 (sample sizes: 51 bvFTD, 14 controls), I6 (performed between-group contrasts of patient groups vs controls), and I7 (reports whole-brain voxelwise group-level results).
